expect_nodes.name: mytool
expect_nodes.note: INTENDED: `subprocess.run(["mytool", "sync"], check=True)` invokes the tool. EXPECTED to miss — cli.rs extract_quoted() requires a quote IMMEDIATELY after the pattern, so the LIST form (the only form that works without shell=True) yields nothing. Only `subprocess.run("mytool sync")` is captured.

expect_edges.note: INTENDED: invocation -> declaration. EXPECTED to miss — there is no invocation node to route from.

forbid.name: sync
forbid.note: precision: the subcommand argument must never be minted as a separate invoked tool

note: ZERO-EVERYWHERE PROBE (A15.11), and a sharply actionable one. Baseline 2026-09-16 on the installed 0.4.18 wheel: 6 nodes / 3 edges, CLI_INVOCATION 0. The gap is one line: cli.rs INVOCATION_PATTERNS matches `subprocess.run(` and then demands a quote, so the canonical Python argv-list call is invisible. cli.rs's own unit test names this — it binds the list form to `_array_form` and asserts on the string form instead.
